Read more Enrission India Capital joins Ottonomy’s Rs 40.6 Cr post-seed funding round Japan-based investor Enrission India Capital has participated in Ottonomy’s Rs 40.6 crore ($4.2 million) post-seed funding round. Ottonomy develops AI-powered autonomous delivery robots capable of operating indoors and outdoors. Its flagship product, Ottobot, uses proprietary Contextual AI to automate the movement of medicines, equipment and supplies across hospitals and industrial facilities. The technology aims to reduce routine logistics workloads amid growing labour shortages, allowing skilled employees to focus on higher-value tasks. The investment will support Ottonomy’s global expansion across healthcare and industrial automation. Enrission India Capital said the investment reflects its focus on deep-tech companies addressing practical business challenges. OneStack raises Rs 12.5 Cr as cooperative banks go live directly on NPCI’s UPI network Fintech infrastructure company OneStack has raised Rs 12.5 crore from new investor Shepherd’s Hill and existing backers Pentathlon Ventures and AVNM Ventures. The funding will support expansion across cooperative banks and NBFCs, alongside product development in payments, core banking and regulatory compliance. OneStack has enabled cooperative banks to operate directly on NPCI’s UPI network as both issuers and acquirers under their own bank handles. This allows banks to issue UPI IDs, onboard merchants, manage transaction data and retain payment-related revenue. The company has raised over Rs 45 crore across four rounds and currently serves more than 200 banks. Its expansion plans include leveraging partnerships covering over 250 cooperative banks and its onboarding as a technology provider on Sahakar Sarathi. Other news Decentro launches static and dynamic QR Soundboxes for merchant payment confirmations Decentro has launched two Soundbox devices to provide instant spoken payment confirmations to merchants. The range includes a Static QR Soundbox and a Dynamic QR Soundbox with a display, keypad and NFC. The static model supports 4G, 2G and optional Wi-Fi, with alerts in English, Hindi and regional languages. The dynamic model generates transaction-specific QR codes and supports contactless card payments through RuPay, Visa and Mastercard, with card functionality expected to go live in around two months. Both devices are available for purchase or rental through banks, fintechs and other platforms. Decentro currently has over 5,000 offline UPI QR codes deployed and targets one million Soundboxes by the end of 2028. (This article will be updated with the latest news throughout the day.)

title: Awfis Q2 profit jumps 93% to Rs 31 Cr, revenue rises to Rs 464 Cr
content: Realty firm Awfis Space Solutions Ltd has reported a 93% increase in its consolidated profit to Rs 30.8 crore for the quarter ended September on higher income amid strong demand for managed workspaces. Its net profit stood at Rs 15.97 crore in the year-ago period. Total income increased to Rs 464.29 crore in the second quarter of this fiscal from Rs 392.97 crore in the year-ago period, according to a regulatory filing on Tuesday. During April-September period of FY27, the company's net profit rose to Rs 54.76 crore from Rs 25.95 crore in the year-ago period. Total income also grew to Rs 913.16 crore in the first six months of this fiscal from Rs 746.01 crore in the corresponding period of the preceding year. Awfis has a presence in 18 cities with more than 250 coworking centres. Amit Ramani, the company's CMD, noted that the company has reported another quarter of steady performance, supported by continued office demand from large enterprises & GCCs (Global Capability Centres) The company continues to focus on premiumisation and operational efficiency, he said. During the September quarter, Ramani said the company has added 6 new centres, taking the total supply to 254 centres with about 1,74,000 seats across 18 cities. The overall portfolio occupancy stood at 76.2%, he said.

title: Peppermint Robotics bags Rs 100 Cr in pre-Series B funding round
content: Peppermint Robotics, which makes autonomous cleaning robots, has raised Rs 100 crore (about $10.5 million) in a pre-Series B round led by pi Ventures and Crane Venture Partners. Asiana Fund also participated in the round. The round involved fresh capital and secondary share transactions. The money arrives on the back of rapid growth by Peppermint. The Pune- and Austin-based startup said it doubled its revenue last year and grew nearly sixfold between FY24 and FY26. It last raised Rs 34 crore ($4 million) in a Series A round in April 2025. Peppermint has a presence in nine countries, with the US being its biggest market. Founded in 2019 at the Society for Innovation and Entrepreneurship at IIT Bombay, the company's autonomous cleaning robots are deployed across a range of commercial and industrial environments, including factories, hospitals, airports, malls, warehouses, hotels and universities. Its machines scrub floors and move materials in factories, hospitals, airports, malls, warehouses, hotels and universities. They are designed to fit into existing routines rather than disrupt workflows. The company primarily serves facility management companies that oversee cleaning operations, including the selection of equipment, chemicals and cleaning processes. One of its more challenging deployments is at a global pharmaceutical company, where its cleanroom robots have passed qualification testing in an EU GMP Grade cleanroom, among the most tightly regulated settings a cleaning robot can enter, Peppermint said, in a statement. Cleanroom robots are specialised manipulators engineered to operate in controlled, contamination-free environments. The startup builds its hardware, software and perception systems in-house and assembles its robots in Pune. They run on proprietary Peppermint OS, using computer vision and LiDAR to map spaces, plan routes, and avoid obstacles. Operators can monitor them in real time through a cloud dashboard. For security-sensitive sites, the company offers fully offline 'stealth' robots that meet stringent information securtiy requirements. Runal Dahiwade, Founder and CEO of Peppermint Robotics, said, "Cleaning teams keep hospitals, factories and airports running. Our robots work alongside them and take on the most repetitive, physically demanding jobs, like floor scrubbing and material transportation. Our customers judge us on one thing: a clean floor, every shift. "So we build our robots heavy-duty, to last multiple years, and we stay with every machine for its whole lifecycle. This round lets us build more of them, closer to our customers worldwide." The newly raised capital will go towards next-generation robotics and expanding manufacturing capacity. An assembly line in North America is also being planned over the coming months. Peppermint also intends to step up business development in the United States and Asia, grow its presence in Europe, and hire senior leaders and engineers. On the product side, it plans to widen its range of floor-cleaning and material-handling robots and develop its cleanroom line. Investors are optimistic about Peppermint's potential and promise. Shubham Sandeep, Partner at pi Ventures, pointed to the company's "clear ROI" in demanding settings such as healthcare and hospitality. Anandamoy Roychowdhary of Crane Venture Partners said Peppermint has built a production-grade cleanroom robot for mission-critical businesses. Neha Aggarwal of Asiana Fund called the company the kind of advanced manufacturing business India can build for global markets. Edited by Swetha Kannan

title: Fractal Analytics net profit more than doubles to Rs 79 Cr in Q2
content: Home-grown AI company Fractal Analytics on Wednesday posted a more than twofold jump in its consolidated profit after tax to Rs 79.2 crore in the second quarter ended September 2026, aided by improved margins, The company had a net profit of Rs 33.2 crore in the same period a year ago, according to a regulatory filing. Consolidated revenue from operations grew by 19.7% to Rs 956.5 crore during the reported quarter from Rs 798.5 crore in the September 2025 quarter. In US dollar terms, this is the first quarter when Fractal has crossed the $100 million mark. Revenue growth was led by the company's Healthcare and Life Sciences (HLS) vertical, which clocked 79% growth YoY, it said. "Banking, Financial Services and Insurance (BFSI) also performed very well, growing 30% YoY in Q2 (second quarter), and the company has delivered strong sustained growth in HLS and BFSI over the last several quarters," the company said. Fractal's largest industry vertical, Consumer Packaged Goods and Retail (CPGR), grew 11% YoY. "AI models are getting more capable every week and cheaper every quarter. Within the next few quarters, we will cross a threshold where it becomes irresponsible and downright risky for companies to leave their most important decisions unchanged. We are building Fractal for that moment, and this quarter shows it: revenue crossed $100 million and net income more than doubled," Fractal Analytics Co-founder and Group CEO Srikanth Velamakanni said.

title: Priyank Kharge asks EV companies to shape Karnataka's growth roadmap
content: Building an electric vehicle ecosystem takes more than putting new vehicles on the road. It also requires battery research, specialised engineering talent, testing facilities and a manufacturing base that can support the industry as it grows. As Karnataka looks to strengthen its position in the EV sector, Minister for Home, Electronics, Information Technology and Biotechnology, and E-Governance Priyank Kharge has asked industry players to help shape a roadmap for the state's electric mobility ecosystem. Ahead of Bengaluru Tech Summit 2026, Kharge held a roundtable with companies and stakeholders from Karnataka's EV industry to understand their priorities, identify areas for collaboration and discuss ways to accelerate the sector's growth. The meeting brought together representatives from Exponent Energy, Ultraviolette, Simple Energy, Sun Mobility, Moonrider and Multiplex EV, alongside other manufacturers, technology companies, battery and energy solutions providers and startups. Building the infrastructure behind electric mobility The discussions covered several areas that could strengthen Karnataka's EV ecosystem, including industry-led research and development, advanced testing and certification facilities, specialised skilling programmes, incubation support and manufacturing infrastructure. Priyank Kharge emphasised that government support should be shaped by the actual requirements of companies operating across the EV value chain. “The government is committed to supporting the growth of the EV sector in Karnataka. However, our interventions must be guided by what the industry actually needs,” he said. He urged companies to come together, identify common priorities and submit a consolidated roadmap to the government. This would help determine which infrastructure and support measures need to be taken forward. Industry to play a role in training EV talent Talent development emerged as another key area during the interaction. As the EV industry expands, companies need specialised professionals across battery technology, embedded systems, firmware, power electronics, vehicle diagnostics, manufacturing and after-sales services. To address this demand, Kharge proposed an industry-backed skilling model in which companies would help design training curricula, certify candidates and provide employment opportunities. The approach would bring employers closer to the training process, helping align the skills being taught with the requirements of the industry. Strengthening local manufacturing capabilities The minister also encouraged companies to explore existing policy incentives available in Karnataka for manufacturing and engineering research and development. The discussions included opportunities to strengthen local manufacturing capabilities and reduce dependence on imports. With the EV industry spanning vehicle production, battery systems, electronics, software and energy infrastructure, Karnataka is looking to bring these capabilities together to support innovation and manufacturing within the state. The roundtable forms part of the state's engagement with industry ahead of Bengaluru Tech Summit 2026, with the proposed roadmap expected to help identify priorities for the next phase of EV ecosystem development.

title: GIVA raises $100M in Multiples-led round; India’s Rs 3 lakh Cr data centre buildout
content: Dear Reader, India’s data centre industry is poised for a five-fold expansion, with installed capacity expected to reach 7.5 GW by March 2030, attracting investments of more than Rs 3 lakh crore over the next four financial years, according to Crisil Ratings. Demand from generative AI, cloud adoption and enterprise digitalisation is driving the build-out. However, power connectivity, regulatory clearances and project execution will be crucial to keeping projects on track. In other news, Bengaluru-based jewellery brand GIVA has raised $100 million in a funding round led by Multiples Alternate Asset Management. The company plans to use the capital to strengthen its leadership team, expand manufacturing and deepen its offline presence. It currently operates more than 400 stores across India and Sri Lanka, selling silver, gold and lab-grown diamond jewellery. Meanwhile, Google has launched Dreambeans , an experimental AI-powered app in India that turns activity across selected services, including Gmail, Calendar, Gemini, Photos, Search and YouTube into personalised stories. Available to users aged 18 and above on Android and iOS, it supports 14 Indian languages. In the drone sector, ideaForge returned to profitability in Q2 FY27, reporting revenue of Rs 91.3 crore, up 124% year-on-year, and a profit after tax of Rs 6.5 crore, against a loss of Rs 19.6 crore a year earlier. Its EBITDA stood at Rs 23.2 crore. Yet progress in business remains uneven. Women hold 30.5% of management positions worldwide, according to an International Labour Organization survey covering companies in 99 countries. Their share has risen only gradually over three decades, despite gains in education, highlighting barriers to career advancement and unequal care responsibilities. In today’s newsletter: India shines in Apple’s record September quarter VC funding into Indian startups plunges 66% in Oct Here’s your trivia for today: Which team holds the record for the most Constructors’ Championships in Formula 1 history? (Scroll down for the answer) News Apple hits record India revenue in September quarter Apple posted its strongest-ever September quarter revenue in India, with the country emerging as a key growth market amid robust demand for its devices. The performance was driven by record iPhone upgrades and Mac sales, alongside the launch of Apple Pay in India. Globally, the tech giant reported quarterly revenue of $114.48 billion, even as rising memory costs and supply constraints weighed on operations. Key takeaways: Apple reported its highest-ever September quarter revenue in India, driven by record iPhone upgrades and strong MacBook demand. Quarterly revenue rose 11.72% year-on-year to $114.48 billion, while FY26 revenue increased 15.06% to a record $478.83 billion. Higher memory prices, advanced chip supply constraints and increased operating expenses put pressure on margins, despite strong iPhone and Services performance. Funding VC funding into Indian startups plunges 66% in October Venture capital funding into Indian startups fell sharply in October, dropping 66% year-on-year to $581 million, according to YourStory Research. The decline was largely driven by the absence of large-value funding rounds, with Even Healthcare's $50 million raise emerging as the month's biggest deal. Despite the subdued month, startups raised $10.4 billion in the first 10 months of 2026, putting the ecosystem on track to match or exceed its 2025 funding total. Key takeaways: Indian startups raised $581 million across 107 deals in October, down 66% from $1.6 billion in October 2025. Even Healthcare’s $50 million round was the biggest deal of the month. Late-stage funding stood at just $97 million, while growth-stage startups raised $250 million. D2C, healthtech and automotive were the top-funded segments. AI startups attracted just $42 million, highlighting the gap in India's AI investment activity. News & updates Gaming: Cricket legend Sachin Tendulkar has joined Hyderabad-based Metasports Interactive, the maker of mobile cricket strategy game Hitwicket, as a strategic investor and brand ambassador. The company, which claims over 20 million users across 120 countries, aims to reach 100 million downloads in three years as it looks to expand its gaming portfolio. Gold demand: India’s gold demand is expected to fall to around 650 tonnes in 2026, its lowest level in six years, as record-high prices dampen jewellery purchases and investment demand. A weak monsoon, rising living costs and pressure on rural incomes are likely to further weigh on buying, despite a potential festive and wedding-season recovery in the December quarter.
